items.q: Treatment of hypercalciuria and hypocitraturia in medullary sponge kidney consists of:
opts: Potassium citrate with increased fluid intake
Alkali restriction with a high-salt diet
items.exp: Treatment in MSK: for hypercalciuria and hypocitraturia — potassium citrate and ↑fluid intake. (Book p792)

items.q: Match each medullary sponge kidney treatment with the abnormality it corrects — 1) Potassium citrate  2) Increased fluid intake  3) The aim of both measures … A) Prevention of recurrent stones  B) Hypocitraturia  C) Hypercalciuria
items.exp: Treatment of MSK: potassium citrate for hypocitraturia and increased fluid intake for hypercalciuria, together preventing recurrent stone formation. (Book p792)

items.q: Match each cause of medullary nephrocalcinosis — 1) Distal RTA  2) Bartter syndrome  3) Sarcoid  4) MSK … A) Sarcoid  B) Bartter syndrome  C) Distal RTA  D) MSK
items.exp: Causes of medullary nephrocalcinosis: distal RTA, Bartter syndrome, sarcoid, MSK, and conditions with hypercalciuria. (Book p792)

items.q: Match each type of nephrocalcinosis with its causes — 1) Medullary  2) Cortical  3) Both medullary and cortical … A) Oxalosis  B) Distal RTA, Bartter syndrome, sarcoid, MSK and conditions with hypercalciuria  C) Tuberculosis and chronic graft rejection
items.exp: Medullary nephrocalcinosis: distal RTA, Bartter syndrome, sarcoid, MSK and hypercalciuric conditions. Cortical nephrocalcinosis: TB and chronic graft rejection. Oxalosis causes both. (Book p792)

items.q: A renal transplant recipient has progressive graft dysfunction with cortical calcification on imaging. Which cause of cortical nephrocalcinosis fits?
items.exp: Cortical nephrocalcinosis causes: tuberculosis and chronic graft rejection (distal RTA, Bartter, sarcoid and MSK cause medullary nephrocalcinosis). (Book p792)

items.q: Oxalosis causes both medullary and cortical nephrocalcinosis.
opts: False — oxalosis causes only medullary nephrocalcinosis
False — oxalosis causes only cortical nephrocalcinosis
items.exp: Note: oxalosis causes both medullary and cortical nephrocalcinosis. (Book p792)

items.q: All but one of the following cause medullary (not cortical) nephrocalcinosis. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Cortical nephrocalcinosis is caused by tuberculosis and chronic graft rejection; distal RTA, Bartter syndrome, sarcoid and MSK cause medullary nephrocalcinosis. (Book p792)

items.q: A patient with MSK has a stone composed of Ca₃(PO₄)₂. Which associated condition explains this stone type?
items.exp: MSK association: incomplete distal RTA in 50% → Ca₃(PO₄)₂ (calcium phosphate) stone. (Book p792)
